title: Add jurisdiction-aware KMS routing, audit watermarking, and RBAC TTL enforcement
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add jurisdiction-aware routing for KMS operations to respect tenant residency claims.
Emit stable audit watermark headers for cross-region request ordering and replay detection.
Introduce RBAC TTL enforcer to allow time-limited elevated operator roles for emergency workflows.
description:
Problem: Customers operating under regulatory constraints needed stronger guarantees that KMS operations are routed to regionally-appropriate key providers and that audit streams carry a stable watermark for cross-region ingestion. Additionally, on-call and operator workflows were requesting time-limited RBAC elevations but we lacked a uniform enforcement layer that prevents stale grants from persisting.

Design summary: This PR implements three coordinated features: (1) a jurisdiction-aware KMS router that matches tenant/residency assertions to KMS provider endpoints with a fallback policy and decision logging; (2) audit watermarking that attaches a monotonic per-tenant watermark header to outgoing persistence events and an ingest-side verifier that rejects out-of-order or duplicate batches; and (3) an RBAC TTL enforcement component that validates and enforces expiration on transient grants issued by the operator escalation service. Each component is gated behind feature flags and defaulted off for existing clusters.

What changed (high level): Added a new KMS routing policy engine (service/kms/router.go + pkg/kms/policy/*), a lightweight decision cache with TTLs to avoid excessive policy evals, an audit watermark generator and verifier (service/audit/watermark.go, service/audit/verifier.go), an RBAC TTL enforcer integrated into the policy evaluation pipeline (pkg/rbac/ttl_enforcer.go), operator-facing migration steps and a k8s overlay for gradual rollout (deploy/k8s/overlays/compliance.yaml). Documentation and API contract notes are under docs/security/kms-routing.md and docs/security/audit-watermarks.md.

Testing: Unit tests added for routing decisions and TTL expiry logic. Integration tests simulate cross-region replay and verify that audit verifier rejects duplicates and that the KMS router falls back to secondary providers when primary is unavailable. Load tests indicate median routing decision latency ~0.7ms under a 1000QPS synthetic policy cache warmup. Security scan coverage added for decision payload serialization.

Rollout plan: Feature flags are controlled through the console and can be enabled per-tenant. Default rollout: internal staging -> select enterprise tenants with consent flag -> global. A migration job is included to backfill recent audit watermark anchors for eligible tenants; job is safe to re-run. In case of routing regressions, there is an automated fallback to legacy KMS behavior controlled by a cluster-level override and monitoring alerts on >0.1% KMS error uplift.

Checklist:
- [x] API + routing policy implementation
- [x] Audit watermark generation + verifier
- [x] RBAC TTL enforcer and integration tests
- [x] Docs and rollout k8s overlays
- [x] Security review and threat-model notes

Related work: This builds on prior policy-compiler changes (ENG-2011) and complements the operator session attestation work (SEC-21).

review_comments: Priya Nair: Can we avoid a synchronous policy fetch on the hot path? Suggest adding a bounded async refresh and a cache hit fallback.
Maya Chen (author): Added a decision cache with 200ms async refresh and bounded staleness; updated router.go to prefer cache and fall back to last-known policy.
Liam O'Connor: The watermark header name needs to be stable across services — suggest X-Redwood-Watermark-V1; watch for proxy stripping.
Maya Chen (author): Renamed header to X-Redwood-Watermark-V1 and added tests for proxy passthrough in ingress simulation.
Arjun Rao: Need a plan for zero-downtime rollback if TTL enforcer blocks an existing long-lived grant; please add an operator override and audit log entry.
Maya Chen (author): Added an operator-override flag and explicit audit entry when a grant is rejected by TTL check. Documented in the operator runbook.
merge_commit_summary: Squash-merged jurisdiction-aware KMS routing, audit watermarking, and RBAC TTL enforcement (feature-flagged).
review_summary: Approved by reviewers after cache/rollback and header naming changes. Security reviewed and approved. Performance impact negligible when cache is warm.
notes_for_ops: Rollback: set cluster override kms.routing.legacy=true and disable feature flags
security_notes: Decision payloads are HMAC-signed to prevent tampering in transit
Watermarks are monotonic per-tenant and include short-lived nonces to prevent replay
user_impact: Enablement is opt-in per-tenant. When enabled, KMS operations will prefer in-region providers; audit ingesters will reject duplicates/out-of-order payloads for tenants with watermarking enabled. RBAC TTL enforcer may reject transient grants that exceed allowed duration; operator override exists.
testing_summary: Unit + integration + replay-fuzzing added. Load test indicates minimal latency impact; see test reports attached in CI artifacts.
additional_context: This PR intentionally keeps behavior behind flags; it is focused on compliancy controls for enterprise customers in regulated jurisdictions. Operators should coordinate with customer success when enabling for tenants with critical KMS constraints.
